svg.title: The computational biology journey of David Jimenez-Morales, PhD
svg.desc: A poster tracing four chapters — Spain, Chicago, San Francisco and Stanford — along a rising path from 1993 to today.
svg.text: A biology degree in Granada, a master's in
computational biology in Madrid, and first
research at the bench: microbes and proteins.
A PhD mapping the hidden cavities inside proteins,
modeling how their sequences evolve, and showing a
chemical tag thought rare was in fact everywhere.
Influenza above all: mapping how the virus rewires
the cells it infects. Computational lead at UCSF and
Gladstone across more than twenty collaborations.
Bioinformatics Lead for four national research
programs: cutting-edge research on exercise and
disease, and the software that makes it possible.
Thirty-three years, four cities, one question: what can molecules tell us about health?
